name: Dunga
milestone_by_age_26: Captained Brazil's U-20 team to victory at the 1983 FIFA U-20 World Cup at age 19, won Olympic silver at the 1984 Los Angeles Games at age 20, and won the 1989 Copa América with Brazil at age 26.
starting_point: Born Carlos Caetano Bledorn Verri on October 31, 1963 in Ijuí, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil to a middle-class family.
current_position: Retired Brazilian footballer and former national team manager; last managed Brazil in 2016; resides in Brazil.

trajectory.title: FIFA U-20 World Cup Champion as Captain
trajectory.description: Captained Brazil's U-20 team to victory at the FIFA U-20 World Cup, beating Argentina in the final.

trajectory.title: Olympic Silver Medalist
trajectory.description: Won silver medal with Brazil at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics football tournament.

trajectory.title: Brazil Senior Team Debut
trajectory.description: Earned his first cap for the Brazil senior national team in a 1-1 draw against England on May 19, 1987.

trajectory.title: Copa América Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Copa América with Brazil, defeating Uruguay in the final held in Rio de Janeiro.

trajectory.title: First World Cup Appearance
trajectory.description: Started for Brazil at the 1990 FIFA World Cup in Italy, though Brazil was eliminated in the Round of 16.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup Champion as Captain
trajectory.description: Captained Brazil to victory at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, beating Italy on penalties in the final.

trajectory.title: World Cup Runner-Up
trajectory.description: Captained Brazil to the final of the 1998 FIFA World Cup in France, losing 3-0 to the host nation.

trajectory.title: Appointed Brazil National Team Manager
trajectory.description: Named head coach of the Brazil national team, leading them through the 2007 Copa América title and 2010 World Cup.

trajectory.title: Second Stint as Brazil Manager
trajectory.description: Reappointed as Brazil national team manager for a second term, lasting until 2016.

name: Jean-Marie Pfaff
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Belgian Golden Shoe as player of the year in 1978 at age 24, won the Belgian Cup with Beveren in 1978, and won the Belgian national championship with Beveren in 1979 at age 25, while also being Belgium's starting goalkeeper from 1976.
starting_point: Born December 4, 1953 in Lebbeke, East Flanders, Belgium; grew up in a caravan park as one of 12 siblings; father was a door-to-door carpet salesman who died when Jean-Marie was 11.
current_position: Retired Belgian football legend; known for reality TV show 'De Pfaffs'; resides in Belgium.

trajectory.title: Professional Debut with Beveren
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut for SK Beveren in the Belgian First Division at the end of the 1971-72 season.

trajectory.title: Became Starting Goalkeeper
trajectory.description: Established himself as Beveren's first-choice goalkeeper under coach Urbain Braems in the 1974-75 season.

trajectory.title: Belgium National Team Debut
trajectory.description: Made his debut for the Belgium national team, beginning a 64-cap international career.

trajectory.title: Belgian Golden Shoe and Cup Winner
trajectory.description: Named Belgian Player of the Year (Golden Shoe) and won the Belgian Cup with Beveren, beating Club Brugge 2-0 in the final.

trajectory.title: Belgian National Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Belgian First Division championship with Beveren, the club's first and only league title.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Signed with Bayern Munich, where he would spend six seasons and become known as 'El Simpático' among fans.

trajectory.title: World Cup All-Star Goalkeeper
trajectory.description: Named to the 1986 FIFA World Cup All-Star Team after helping Belgium reach the semifinals and finish fourth.

trajectory.title: First IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper
trajectory.description: Became the first recipient of the IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper award.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Professional Football
trajectory.description: Retired after a final season with Trabzonspor in Turkey, ending a career spanning 595 club appearances.

name: Fabio Cannavaro
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Napoli in 1993 at age 19, then won the UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma by 1999 (age 25-26), and became an Italy international in 1997, all well before age 26.
starting_point: Born September 13, 1973 in Naples, Italy to a bank clerk father who also played football for Giugliano and a mother who worked as a maid.
current_position: Head coach of the Uzbekistan national team as of 2025; former Ballon d'Or winner and World Cup champion defender.

trajectory.title: Training with Napoli First Team
trajectory.description: Spotted by Napoli scouts as a teenager and trained with the first team, marking Maradona in practice sessions.

trajectory.title: Serie A Debut for Napoli
trajectory.description: Made his Serie A debut for Napoli, beginning his professional career in Italy's top flight.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Parma
trajectory.description: Joined Parma, where he would spend seven seasons and form one of Europe's most formidable defensive units.

trajectory.title: Italy National Team Debut
trajectory.description: Made his international debut for Italy against Northern Ireland in Palermo in January 1997.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia Double
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma, establishing himself as one of the world's elite center-backs.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Inter Milan
trajectory.description: Moved to Inter Milan for two seasons before joining Juventus under Fabio Capello in 2004.

trajectory.title: World Cup Champion and Ballon d'Or Winner
trajectory.description: Captained Italy to the 2006 FIFA World Cup title and won the Ballon d'Or, the only defender to receive it in the 2000s decade.

trajectory.title: La Liga Champion with Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Won consecutive La Liga titles with Real Madrid in 2007 and 2008 after transferring from Juventus.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Playing
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after a stint with Al-Ahli in Dubai, ending a 694-match club career.

trajectory.title: Appointed Head Coach of Uzbekistan
trajectory.description: Named head coach of the Uzbekistan national team after previous managerial roles in China, Italy, and Croatia.

name: Philip Meng
milestone_by_age_26: Accepted to YC S26 as CEO of Shepherd while a high school senior, receiving $500K in funding.
starting_point: High school student in the United States; founded Launchpad, a startup incubator for high schoolers, in 9th grade.
current_position: Founder & CEO of Shepherd (YC S26), based in San Francisco; deferred Stanford and Harvard to pursue the startup.

trajectory.title: Founded Launchpad
trajectory.description: Co-founded Launchpad, a global startup and non-profit incubator for high schoolers that helped found 37 startups.

trajectory.title: AI Research Publications
trajectory.description: Published three papers at top AI conferences on LLM bias and low-resource languages, including the AAVENUE benchmark.

trajectory.title: Launched The Early Founder Podcast
trajectory.description: Started a podcast interviewing young founders, building connections in the startup ecosystem.

trajectory.title: Investment Intern at 645 Ventures
trajectory.description: Worked as an investment intern at 645 Ventures, gaining VC experience while in high school.

trajectory.title: Accepted to YC S26 with Shepherd
trajectory.description: Co-founded Shepherd with Ishan Ramrakhiani and Elijah Renner; accepted to Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, receiving $500K in funding instead of attending Stanford or Harvard.

name: Ishan Ramrakhiani
milestone_by_age_26: Accepted to YC S26 as CPO of Shepherd while a high school senior, receiving $500K in funding.
starting_point: High school student from Indiana; developed research tools and AI projects throughout high school.
current_position: Founder & CPO of Shepherd (YC S26); deferred Stanford to pursue the startup.

trajectory.title: Built Research Mentor Matching Tool
trajectory.description: Developed a tool to help students find research mentors that grew to 60,000 users.

trajectory.title: AI Video Editing Agent
trajectory.description: Developed an AI video editing agent inside Adobe After Effects as a side project.

trajectory.title: Research at Dartmouth
trajectory.description: Spent summers in labs exploring breath sensors for disease detection, molecular models for drug discovery, and virtual RNA inference models at Dartmouth.

trajectory.title: Continued Building and Preparing for YC
trajectory.description: Continued developing AI projects and exploring startup opportunities while preparing to apply to Y Combinator with co-founders Philip Meng and Elijah Renner.

trajectory.title: Accepted to YC S26 with Shepherd
trajectory.description: Co-founded Shepherd as CPO with Philip Meng and Elijah Renner; accepted to Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, receiving $500K in funding instead of attending Stanford.

trajectory.title: Building Shepherd Full-Time
trajectory.description: Building Shepherd full-time in San Francisco after YC acceptance, focusing on product development and customer growth.

name: Abbas Sajwani
milestone_by_age_26: Founded AHS Group in 2017 at age 18 and launched AHS Properties in 2021 at age 22, building a multi-billion-dollar luxury real estate development company in Dubai; named to Forbes Middle East 30 Under 30 in 2024 and became the youngest Arab billionaire in 2026.
starting_point: Born July 22, 1999 in Dubai, UAE; son of billionaire developer Hussain Sajwani, founder of DAMAC Properties.
current_position: Founder & CEO of AHS Properties; youngest Arab billionaire with net worth of $1.9 billion as of 2026.

trajectory.title: Founded AHS Group
trajectory.description: Established AHS Group as a platform for investments and entrepreneurial ventures across multiple sectors in Dubai.

trajectory.title: Stock Trading Profits
trajectory.description: Made a small fortune trading Simon Property Group stock during a period of global market volatility between 2020 and 2021.

trajectory.title: Launched AHS Properties
trajectory.description: Formally launched AHS Properties at Cityscape Global 2021, initially acquiring and renovating luxury villas in Palm Jumeirah and Emirates Hills.

trajectory.title: First Off-Plan Development
trajectory.description: Launched One Canal, AHS Properties' first off-plan development along the Dubai Water Canal.

trajectory.title: Expanded Portfolio
trajectory.description: Launched One Crescent on Palm Jumeirah and announced Casa Canal; combined asset value estimated at $1.65 billion; named to Arabian Business 100 Most Influential Arabs.

trajectory.title: Forbes Middle East 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Named to Forbes Middle East's 30 Under 30 list; AHS Properties ranked Dubai's top developer for transactions.

trajectory.title: Acquired Big Ben Tower
trajectory.description: Purchased Dubai's long-vacant Big Ben tower for $120 million on Sheikh Zayed Road, rebranding it as AHS Tower for commercial real estate.

trajectory.title: Youngest Arab Billionaire
trajectory.description: Named by Forbes as the youngest Arab billionaire and youngest real estate billionaire globally, with a net worth of $1.9 billion.

name: Yu Wenbo
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2018 League of Legends World Championship with Invictus Gaming at age 17, becoming the first Chinese bot laner to win Worlds and the first LPL team to claim the title.
starting_point: Born November 18, 2000 in China; began playing League of Legends competitively as a teenager.
current_position: Bot laner for Top Esports (TES) in the LPL; one of China's most accomplished League of Legends players with over $4.2M in career prize money.

trajectory.title: Joined Invictus Gaming
trajectory.description: Signed with Invictus Gaming's roster, beginning his professional League of Legends career.

trajectory.title: Stint with Young Glory
trajectory.description: Briefly played for Young Glory before returning to Invictus Gaming's main roster in May 2017.

trajectory.title: World Championship Winner
trajectory.description: Won the 2018 League of Legends World Championship with Invictus Gaming, sweeping Fnatic 3-0 in the final; first LPL team and first Chinese bot laner to win Worlds.

trajectory.title: Worlds Semifinalist
trajectory.description: Reached the semifinals (3rd-4th) of the 2019 World Championship with Invictus Gaming before leaving the team in November.

trajectory.title: Joined Top Esports
trajectory.description: Signed with Top Esports in April 2020, becoming the team's starting bot laner.

trajectory.title: Continued LPL Dominance
trajectory.description: Continued competing at the highest level with Top Esports, remaining one of the LPL's premier bot laners with over $4.2M in career earnings.

name: Danil Kryshkovets
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024 with Team Spirit at age 17, becoming the youngest-ever CS Major champion and MVP while recording the highest individual rating ever at a Major.
starting_point: Born January 25, 2007 in Tomsk, Russia; scouted at age 14 by Team Spirit's talent pipeline.
current_position: Rifler for Team Spirit in Counter-Strike 2; named HLTV Player of the Year 2024 at age 17, the youngest ever.

trajectory.title: Scouted by Team Spirit Academy
trajectory.description: Discovered by Aleksey 'OverDrive' Biryukov and invited to join Team Spirit's youth roster.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Team Spirit Main Roster
trajectory.description: Moved up to Team Spirit's main CS2 roster in July; won first tournament (CCT North Europe Series #6) and earned first HLTV MVP at BetBoom Dacha Dubai.

trajectory.title: IEM Katowice Champion
trajectory.description: Won IEM Katowice 2024 with Team Spirit, earning MVP honors and establishing himself as a top-tier player.

trajectory.title: Youngest-Ever CS Major Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024 with Team Spirit, becoming the youngest-ever Major champion and MVP with the highest individual rating ever at a Major.

trajectory.title: HLTV Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Named HLTV Player of the Year at 17 years and 352 days old, the youngest ever to receive the award; also named Rookie of the Year and Opener of the Year.

trajectory.title: IEM Cologne Champion
trajectory.description: Won IEM Cologne 2025 and multiple BLAST Bounty titles, continuing his dominant run with Team Spirit.

name: Valerii Vakhovskyi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the PGL Major Stockholm 2021 with Natus Vincere at age 18, also becoming the youngest Intel Grand Slam winner at 18 years and 250 days old.
starting_point: Born January 5, 2003 in Dnipro, Ukraine; joined NAVI's youth pipeline through the Esports Camp program.
current_position: Rifler for Natus Vincere (NAVI) in Counter-Strike 2; two-time Major winner with over $4.9M in career prize money.

trajectory.title: Joined NAVI Junior
trajectory.description: Joined Natus Vincere's Junior team after standout performance at NAVI's Esports Camp; first notable success with team NOTBAD at CIS Minor qualifiers.

trajectory.title: Promoted to NAVI Main Roster
trajectory.description: Became the sixth player of Natus Vincere's CS:GO team in December 2020, initially substituting for flamie on Inferno.

trajectory.title: PGL Major Stockholm Champion
trajectory.description: Won PGL Major Stockholm 2021 with NAVI, going undefeated through the tournament; set record for highest average headshots per round at a Major.

trajectory.title: Youngest Intel Grand Slam Winner
trajectory.description: Became the youngest Intel Grand Slam winner at 18 years and 250 days old after NAVI won four ESL/DreamHack events in a season.

trajectory.title: BLAST Premier World Final Champion
trajectory.description: Won BLAST Premier World Final 2021 and Fall Finals 2021 with NAVI, capping a dominant year.

trajectory.title: BLAST Premier Spring Finals Champion
trajectory.description: Won BLAST Premier Spring Finals 2022 with NAVI; named to HLTV Top 20 players for the second consecutive year.

trajectory.title: PGL Major Copenhagen Champion
trajectory.description: Won his second CS2 Major at PGL Major Copenhagen 2024 with NAVI; also won Esports World Cup 2024 and ESL Pro League Season 20.

name: Anathan Pham
milestone_by_age_26: Won The International 2018 with OG at age 18, then repeated as champion in 2019, becoming part of the first team to win back-to-back TI titles and developing a novel carry Io strategy that revolutionized the meta.
starting_point: Born October 26, 1999 in Melbourne, Australia; dropped out of high school at age 16 and moved to Shanghai to pursue professional Dota 2.
current_position: Retired from professional Dota 2; last played for T1 in 2022; resides in Australia.

trajectory.title: Moved to Shanghai for Pro Gaming
trajectory.description: Dropped out of high school and moved to Shanghai to join Invictus Gaming's in-house league as a substitute for Ferrari_430.

trajectory.title: Joined OG and Won Boston Major
trajectory.description: Left iG to join European team OG; won the Boston Major in December 2016, his first major championship.

trajectory.title: Kiev Major Champion
trajectory.description: Won his second Dota Major at the Kiev Major with OG in April 2017 before taking a break after TI7.

trajectory.title: The International 2018 Champion
trajectory.description: Returned to OG and won The International 2018, the largest prize pool in esports history at the time, earning over $2.2M in prize money.

trajectory.title: Back-to-Back TI Champion
trajectory.description: Won The International 2019 with OG, becoming part of the first team to win back-to-back TI titles; earned over $3.1M in prize money.

trajectory.title: Brief Return to OG
trajectory.description: Returned to OG briefly for The International 2021 qualifiers cycle before going on another hiatus.

trajectory.title: Final Stint with T1
trajectory.description: Joined T1 for a brief period in 2022 but failed to qualify for The International; subsequently retired from professional Dota 2.

name: Saul Leonardo Mena II
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Capcom Cup 2017 at age 18, defeating reigning EVO champion Tokido in the grand finals to claim the $250,000 first prize, the largest ever awarded at a fighting game tournament at the time.
starting_point: Born in the Dominican Republic; began playing fighting games at a small game center in Santo Domingo with unreliable power; inspired by his older brother's interest in fighting games.
current_position: Professional Street Fighter player; four-time EVO champion and two-time Capcom Cup champion; one of the greatest Street Fighter players in history.

trajectory.title: First Competitive Appearance
trajectory.description: Secured a joint-5th place finish at Fighting Fest 2015, his first notable competitive result in Street Fighter.

trajectory.title: Northeast Championship Runner-Up
trajectory.description: Finished second at Northeast Championship 17 in Pennsylvania, defeating Justin Wong and NuckleDu en route; began Capcom Pro Tour run.

trajectory.title: Signed by Rise Nation
trajectory.description: Won Game Over Tournament 2017 in Santo Domingo, his first CPT Ranking Event win, and was signed by esports organization Rise Nation shortly after.

trajectory.title: Capcom Cup 2017 Champion
trajectory.description: Won Capcom Cup 2017 by defeating reigning EVO champion Tokido in a grand finals bracket reset, claiming $250,000; first Latin-American player to win the Capcom Cup.

trajectory.title: Second Capcom Cup Championship
trajectory.description: Won Capcom Cup IX, becoming the only player to ever win the Capcom Cup twice; defeated rising stars EndingWalker and Zhen in the process.

trajectory.title: EVO Japan Champion
trajectory.description: Won EVO Japan 2024 in Street Fighter 6, adding to his growing list of major titles.

trajectory.title: EVO 2025 Champion
trajectory.description: Won EVO 2025 in Las Vegas and EVO Japan 2025, becoming a four-time EVO champion and the most dominant Street Fighter 6 player in the world.

name: Allan Alvarez
milestone_by_age_26: Set the world record in Super Mario 64 120-star category in May 2017 at age 22, becoming the first person to complete the category in under 100 minutes, and held the record on multiple occasions.
starting_point: Born February 26, 1995 in Venezuela; grew up in Trinidad where he discovered speedrunning videos on YouTube as a teenager.
current_position: Full-time Super Mario 64 speedrunner and Twitch streamer; one of the greatest SM64 players of all time.

trajectory.title: Began Speedrunning Super Mario 64
trajectory.description: Discovered speedrunning videos on YouTube in Trinidad and began attempting his own runs of Super Mario 64.

trajectory.title: Started Twitch Streaming
trajectory.description: Began streaming SM64 speedruns nightly on Twitch after graduating high school, earning about $100-200 per month initially.

trajectory.title: First World Record
trajectory.description: Achieved his first world record in the SM64 120-star category, landing $1,000 in donations that day.

trajectory.title: First Sub-100 Minute 120-Star Run
trajectory.description: Became the first person to complete a 120-star run in under 100 minutes with a time of 1:39:57, breaking a record many thought impossible.

trajectory.title: Personal Best 1:38:25
trajectory.description: Set a personal best time of 1:38:25 in the 120-star category, continuing to push the boundaries of the game.

trajectory.title: Reclaimed World Record at 1:37:50
trajectory.description: Reclaimed the world record with a run of 1:37:50, becoming the second person in history to break the 1:38 barrier.

name: Alex Tan
milestone_by_age_26: Set the world record for speedrunning Super Mario World in 2015 at age 19, completing the game in 1 minute and 38 seconds using arbitrary code execution, and created the Guinness World Record-holding most difficult level in Super Mario Maker.
starting_point: Born March 13, 1996 in Rocky Hill, Connecticut; discovered ROM hacking through a YouTube video in 2007 and joined the SMW Central community.
current_position: Full-time Twitch streamer and Mario level designer; known for creating the most difficult Super Mario Maker levels ever made.

trajectory.title: Began ROM Hacking Super Mario World
trajectory.description: Discovered Kaizo Mario World on YouTube and joined smwcentral.net, beginning to create custom levels using Lunar Magic.

trajectory.title: Super Mario World Speedrun World Record
trajectory.description: Set the world record for speedrunning Super Mario World, completing the game in 1 minute and 38 seconds using arbitrary code execution.

trajectory.title: Completed Super Mario World Blindfolded
trajectory.description: Completed a full blindfolded run of Super Mario World in 23 minutes, memorizing routes using musical cues from the game.

trajectory.title: Guinness World Record for Hardest Mario Maker Level
trajectory.description: Created 'Pit of Panga: U-Break' in Super Mario Maker, certified by Guinness World Records as the most difficult level ever created in the game.

trajectory.title: Reclaimed Blindfolded World Record
trajectory.description: Reclaimed the blindfolded Super Mario World world record with a time of 15:59 using the Japanese release.

trajectory.title: Graduated from University of Connecticut
trajectory.description: Graduated from UConn School of Business with a degree in Management Information Systems.

trajectory.title: Super Mario Maker 2 Content Creator
trajectory.description: Became one of the most prominent Kaizo level creators in Super Mario Maker 2, creating levels like Skyzo and P-Break that influenced the entire community.

name: Kennedy Ekezie
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Kippa, a fintech bookkeeping platform for African SMEs, in 2021 at age 23, which raised over $11.6M and onboarded 800,000+ businesses; also received Queen's Young Leader Award from Queen Elizabeth II in 2018 at age 20.
starting_point: Born June 11, 1998 in Lagos, Nigeria; raised in Calabar; graduated as the youngest-ever student from the University of Calabar at age 19.
current_position: Founder & CEO of Kippa/Waymaker; based in Lagos, Nigeria; Forbes 30 Under 30 (North America) honoree.

trajectory.title: Founded Calabar Youth Council for Women's Rights
trajectory.description: Founded an organization to promote women's rights after discovering over 8,000 women are victims of FGM in Nigeria.

trajectory.title: Youngest-Ever University Graduate
trajectory.description: Graduated as the youngest-ever student from the University of Calabar at age 19; selected as Global Teen Leader by We Are Family Foundation; received Obama's Young African Leaders Fellowship.

trajectory.title: Queen's Young Leader Award
trajectory.description: Received the Queen's Young Leader Award from Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace; awarded Yenching Scholarship (China's Rhodes Scholarship) to study at Peking University.

trajectory.title: Built TikTok's Africa Strategy at ByteDance
trajectory.description: Worked at ByteDance's Beijing HQ, credited as part of the team that led TikTok's expansion into Africa.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Kippa
trajectory.description: Co-founded Kippa, a fintech bookkeeping platform for African SMEs; the app onboarded 800,000+ businesses and raised over $11.6M in funding.

trajectory.title: The Future Awards Africa Prize for Technology
trajectory.description: Won The Future Awards Africa Prize for Technology for his work as a technology entrepreneur with Kippa.

trajectory.title: Forbes 30 Under 30 (North America)
trajectory.description: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 list in Finance for Kippa's impact on African small businesses.

name: Hany Rashwan
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Payout.com, an enterprise fintech company, in late 2014 at age 24, which processed over $50M in loans by its second year and raised $4.75M led by Tim Draper; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2017.
starting_point: Born May 7, 1990 in Cairo, Egypt; moved to the United States; attended Ohio State University before transferring to Columbia University.
current_position: Co-founder of 21.co (parent of 21Shares), a cryptocurrency company; based in Zurich, Switzerland.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Ohio State University
trajectory.description: Began studying economics and computer science at Ohio State University before transferring to Columbia University.

trajectory.title: Founded Ribbon
trajectory.description: Founded social commerce company Ribbon, which built the first in-stream 'buy buttons' on Twitter and Facebook.

trajectory.title: Founded Payout.com
trajectory.description: Left Columbia University to found Payout.com, an enterprise fintech providing payouts and compliance APIs for online lenders.

trajectory.title: AngelPad Accelerator
trajectory.description: Payout.com completed the AngelPad accelerator program and began processing loans for clients like LendUp and Prosper.

trajectory.title: Raised $4.75M for Payout.com
trajectory.description: Payout.com raised $4.75M led by Tim Draper of Draper Associates; processed over $50M in loans by its second year.

trajectory.title: Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Named to the 2017 Forbes 30 Under 30 list in Enterprise Technology for Payout.com.

trajectory.title: Co-founded 21Shares
trajectory.description: Co-founded 21Shares (now 21.co), a cryptocurrency ETP company based in Zurich, Switzerland.

trajectory.title: 21.co Growth
trajectory.description: 21.co/21Shares became one of the world's leading crypto ETP providers, with billions in assets under management.

name: Ferry Unardi
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Traveloka, Southeast Asia's largest online travel agency, in March 2012 at age 24 after leaving Harvard Business School, launching the platform publicly in October 2012.
starting_point: Born January 16, 1988 in Padang, Indonesia; developed interest in IT through programming competitions in high school; moved to the US in 2004.
current_position: CEO & Co-founder of Traveloka, Southeast Asia's largest online travel agency; recipient of the Satyalancana Wira Karya Award from the President of Indonesia.

trajectory.title: Moved to the United States
trajectory.description: Graduated high school in Padang and moved to the US to attend Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Purdue and Joined Microsoft
trajectory.description: Earned BS degrees in Computer Science and Mathematics from Purdue; moved to Seattle to work as a software engineer at Microsoft on Microsoft Lync.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Harvard Business School
trajectory.description: Resigned from Microsoft and enrolled at Harvard Business School for an MBA; explored e-commerce companies in China including Alibaba, Ctrip, and Qunar.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Traveloka
trajectory.description: Co-founded Traveloka in March 2012 with Derianto Kusuma and Albert Zhang; left Harvard to focus on the startup full-time.

trajectory.title: Traveloka Public Launch
trajectory.description: Launched Traveloka publicly in October 2012; received initial funding from East Ventures one month after launch.

trajectory.title: Traveloka Achieved Unicorn Status
trajectory.description: Traveloka reached a valuation of $3 billion, becoming one of Southeast Asia's most prominent unicorn startups.

trajectory.title: Largest OTA in Southeast Asia
trajectory.description: Traveloka became the largest online travel agency in Southeast Asia, expanding to 20+ countries with over 100 million users.

name: Ella Langley
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, her debut single 'You Look Like You Love Me' with Riley Green reached #1 on the Billboard Country Airplay chart and won Musical Event of the Year at the CMA Awards (November 2024).
starting_point: Born May 3, 1999 in Hope Hull, Alabama; grew up on a farm in a musically inclined family; learned to read from a hymnal.
current_position: Country music star; signed to Sony Music Nashville and Columbia Records; multiple CMA and ACM award winner.

trajectory.title: First Song Written
trajectory.description: Co-wrote her first song 'Clear the Clouds' with her aunt, recording it at Guest House Studios in Eclectic, Alabama.

trajectory.title: Released Debut Single
trajectory.description: Released her debut single 'Perfect' on May 24, 2018, while performing across Alabama at bars and festivals.

trajectory.title: Moved to Nashville
trajectory.description: Dropped out of Auburn University (where she studied forestry) and relocated to Nashville to pursue music full-time.

trajectory.title: TikTok Viral and Publishing Deal
trajectory.description: Went viral on TikTok with 'If You Have To' filmed inside a car; secured her first publishing deal with Sony Music Publishing Nashville.

trajectory.title: Signed to Columbia Records
trajectory.description: Signed with Columbia Records/SAWGOD in June 2022; began touring as an opener for Randy Houser and other country artists.

trajectory.title: Debut EP and Grand Ole Opry
trajectory.description: Released debut EP 'Excuse the Mess' which exceeded 120 million streams in under a year; debuted at the Grand Ole Opry.

trajectory.title: #1 Country Airplay Hit and CMA Winner

trajectory.description: Formed the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy with John Higgins and Martin Herlihy while students at NYU; performed monthly shows at The Peoples Improv Theatre.

trajectory.title: New York Comedy Festival
trajectory.description: Performed at the New York Comedy Festival; began posting sketch videos on YouTube and later TikTok and Twitter during COVID.

trajectory.title: Hired as SNL Writer
trajectory.description: Hired as a writer for SNL's 47th season with Higgins and Herlihy; debuted with 'Hard Seltzer' sketch on October 9, 2021.

trajectory.title: 'Three Sad Virgins' Goes Viral
trajectory.description: The PDD sketch 'Three Sad Virgins' featuring Pete Davidson and Taylor Swift received widespread attention, launching the trio to fame.

trajectory.title: Film and National Tour
trajectory.description: Wrote and starred in 'Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain' on Peacock (executive produced by Judd Apatow); completed a 26-date U.S. comedy tour.

trajectory.title: Promoted to SNL Cast Member
trajectory.description: Promoted from writer to featured player on SNL's Season 51 in September 2025; guest-starred in Poker Face Season 2; cast in Kevin Hart's Netflix film '72 Hours'.

name: John Higgins
milestone_by_age_26: Was hired as a writer for Saturday Night Live's 47th season in 2021 at age 25 as part of the Please Don't Destroy comedy trio, producing viral pre-recorded sketches for the show.
starting_point: Born November 14, 1995 in Montclair, New Jersey; son of Steve Higgins, SNL writer-producer since 1995 and announcer on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon; attended NYU studying acting and English.
current_position: Comedian and actor; left SNL in September 2025 to pursue acting opportunities; continues working with Please Don't Destroy on tour and new projects.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Please Don't Destroy
trajectory.description: Formed the comedy trio with Ben Marshall and Martin Herlihy at NYU; began performing monthly shows at The Peoples Improv Theatre in Gramercy.

trajectory.title: Hired as SNL Writer
trajectory.description: Hired as a writer for SNL's 47th season with Marshall and Herlihy; debuted with 'Hard Seltzer' sketch on October 9, 2021.

trajectory.title: 'Three Sad Virgins' Goes Viral
trajectory.description: The PDD sketch featuring Pete Davidson and Taylor Swift launched the trio to national fame; produced 39 digital shorts across four SNL seasons.

trajectory.title: Film and National Tour
trajectory.description: Co-wrote and starred in 'Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain' on Peacock; completed a 26-date U.S. comedy tour.

trajectory.title: Left SNL to Pursue Acting
trajectory.description: Announced departure from SNL in September 2025 to pursue acting opportunities; continues touring with Please Don't Destroy and developing new film projects.

name: Joseph Sissens
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to Principal Dancer at The Royal Ballet in June 2024 at age 25, becoming one of the few dancers of colour to reach the top rank at Covent Garden.
starting_point: Born December 26, 1998 at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge, England to a British mother and Jamaican father; grew up in Hertfordshire as one of six siblings; discovered dance accompanying his sister to ballet class.
current_position: Principal Dancer at The Royal Ballet, Covent Garden, London; first person of Black heritage to perform a principal role in Swan Lake for The Royal Ballet.

trajectory.title: Scholarship at Tring Park School
trajectory.description: Awarded a scholarship at Tring Park School for the Performing Arts, where he trained for five years in dance and performance.

trajectory.title: Entered The Royal Ballet School
trajectory.description: Accepted into The Royal Ballet School at age 13 on scholarship, training in classical ballet.

trajectory.title: Joined The Royal Ballet
trajectory.description: Graduated from the Royal Ballet School and joined The Royal Ballet company as an Artist.

trajectory.title: Promoted to First Artist
trajectory.description: Earned his first promotion to First Artist; made his soloist debut in Ashton's 'Symphonic Variations' at age 19.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Soloist
trajectory.description: Promoted to Soloist at The Royal Ballet; won the Black British Theatre Award for Best Dance Performance.

trajectory.title: Promoted to First Soloist
trajectory.description: Promoted to First Soloist; known for roles including Mercutio and Romeo in Romeo and Juliet, and Lensky in Onegin.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Principal Dancer
trajectory.description: Promoted to Principal Dancer by director Kevin O'Hare; curated the inaugural 'Legacy' gala celebrating Black and Brown excellence in ballet for Black History Month.

name: Chloe Misseldine
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to Principal Dancer at American Ballet Theatre in July 2024 at age 22, after her New York debut as Odette/Odile in Swan Lake at the Metropolitan Opera House.
starting_point: Born in Orlando, Florida; mother Yan Chen was an ABT soloist and ballet mistress at Orlando Ballet; grew up in the studio while her mother worked; attended ABT Summer Intensives as a National Training Scholar.
current_position: Principal Dancer at American Ballet Theatre; one of the youngest principals in ABT history.

trajectory.title: Performed at CCTV New Year's Gala
trajectory.description: Performed a traditional Chinese fan dance 'Mo Li Hua' at the CCTV New Year's Gala (Beijing Spring Festival Gala), broadcast to over 700 million viewers.

trajectory.title: YAGP Second Place
trajectory.description: Earned second place in the 2017 Youth America Grand Prix New York City Finals and performed at the YAGP 'Stars of Today Meet the Stars of Tomorrow' Gala.

trajectory.title: Prix de Lausanne Finalist and ABT Studio Company
trajectory.description: Named a finalist at the Prix de Lausanne in Switzerland; joined American Ballet Theatre's Studio Company.

trajectory.title: ABT Apprentice
trajectory.description: Became an apprentice with the main ABT company in December 2019; pandemic forced her back to Orlando where she performed with Orlando Ballet.

trajectory.title: Joined ABT Corps de Ballet
trajectory.description: Joined the Corps de Ballet of American Ballet Theatre by September 2021 after returning from pandemic.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Soloist
trajectory.description: Promoted to the rank of Soloist at ABT in September 2022, just one year after joining the corps.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Principal Dancer
trajectory.description: Promoted to Principal Dancer by director Susan Jaffe on stage after her New York debut as Odette/Odile in Swan Lake at the Metropolitan Opera House in a sold-out performance.

name: Philip Kim
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold at the 2022 WDSF World Breaking Championships in Seoul, South Korea, beating over 250 competitors to become world champion at age 25.
starting_point: Born January 25, 1997 in Vancouver, Canada; Korean heritage; discovered breaking in 2009 at age 12 when he saw the N.O.N. crew performing street shows in downtown Vancouver.
current_position: Olympic gold medalist in breaking (Paris 2024); world champion breakdancer known as B-Boy Phil Wizard; based in Vancouver, Canada.

trajectory.title: Discovered Breaking
trajectory.description: Saw the Now or Never (N.O.N.) crew performing street shows in downtown Vancouver and began learning breaking through YouTube videos.

trajectory.title: Red Bull BC One National Championship
trajectory.description: Entered the inaugural Canadian Red Bull BC One national championship, losing in the final round to Fléau of Montreal.

trajectory.title: First Canadian to Win Undisputed World Series
trajectory.description: Made history as the first Canadian to win the Undisputed World Series with his victory at the Undisputed V Masters in Morocco.

trajectory.title: World Breaking Championship Silver
trajectory.description: Won silver at the 2021 WDSF World Breaking Championships in Paris, establishing himself as a top international competitor.

trajectory.title: World Breaking Champion
trajectory.description: Won gold at the 2022 WDSF World Breaking Championships in Seoul, South Korea, beating over 250 competitors including Shigekix in the final.

trajectory.title: Pan American Games Gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the 2023 Pan American Games in Santiago, Chile, becoming the first-ever b-boy Pan Am Games champion; also won silver at 2023 World Championships.

trajectory.title: Olympic Gold Medal
trajectory.description: Won gold in the inaugural Olympic breaking competition at the 2024 Paris Olympics, cementing his legacy as the sport's greatest champion.

name: Slavik Pustovoytov
milestone_by_age_26: Placed fourth as a finalist on the fifteenth season of So You Think You Can Dance in 2018 at age 19, gaining nationwide recognition in the dance community.
starting_point: Born December 23, 1998 in Poltava, Ukraine; moved to the United States at age 13, leaving his family in Ukraine; settled in Oklahoma before moving to Las Vegas where he discovered dance.
current_position: Dancer, actor, model, and social media influencer known as Viktor 'Vik' White; based in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: So You Think You Can Dance Finalist
trajectory.description: Competed on Season 15 of So You Think You Can Dance as a hip-hop dancer, placing 4th overall and gaining nationwide recognition.

trajectory.title: Post-SYTYCD Career Growth
trajectory.description: Leveraged SYTYCD fame to build a career in dance, appearing in interviews and building a social media following.

trajectory.title: Film Debut in 'He's All That'
trajectory.description: Appeared in the Netflix film 'He's All That' (2021), beginning his transition from dancer to actor.

trajectory.title: Film Roles and Influencer Growth
trajectory.description: Appeared in films '10 Eyes' (2022) and 'Prisoner's Daughter' (2022); built a significant following as a social media influencer under the name Viktor 'Vik' White.

trajectory.title: Hollywood Career
trajectory.description: Continued building his career in Hollywood as a dancer, actor, model, and influencer, known in dance culture on social media.
